text:
sara: quick proposal — 'probe-slice' protocol for cross-variant quant bakeoffs. goal: small, deterministic slices that surface model-architecture x quantization interactions (fp8/int8/gptq/awq).

mia: love this. can we make slices stable across model versions and prompt ordering? that's been messy in previous runs. :eyes:

sara: yes — core constraints: (1) deterministic seed + frozen shuffle, (2) de-dup at canonical normalized text, (3) stratify by prompt length, task type, and hallucination risk.

alex: can you sketch the slice schema? short example pls.

sara: yes, rough schema below — each slice is ~500 probes (target), smaller debug slices exist for fast iteration.

```json
{
  "slice_id": "dialog_short_factual_01",
  "seed": 42,
  "filters": {
    "min_tokens": 8,
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "task_tag": "factual_qa",
    "source_whitelist": ["internal-qbank-v2","web-crawl-2023"]
  },
  "dedupe_normalization": true,
  "negative_controls": "paraphrase_negatives_v1",
  "size_target": 500
}
```

jin: negative controls — do you mean explicit adversarial paraphrases and empty-context cases?

sara: yes. two types: (A) paraphrase-negatives to measure sensitivity to small wording shifts; (B) instruction-less/empty-context to catch spurious generation. both labelled and included in stratified holdouts.

dmitri: how do we pick which prompts go into the calibration vs. holdout evaluation sets? previous calibrations introduced selection bias.

sara: proposed: rolling-window selection. pick N per stratum for calibration (e.g., 100 per length/task strata) with matched holdouts drawn from same strata but different seed range. log split and persist IDs so we can recompute.

alex: scoring — what's the metric suite? aggregate + per-slice deltas?

mia: must include: exact-match (where applicable), BLEU/ROUGE for generative tasks, logprob delta, and a hallucination/incorrectness binary label for factual tasks. compute per-slice mean delta and 95% bootstrap CI.

jin: runtime profiling too? we should tie accuracy deltas to per-token latency and memory for each quant variant.

sara: absolutely — every run should attach a profile artifact: p99 latency, steady throughput, peak GPU memory, and token-cost estimate. we'll keep a small standardized workload generator for that.

eval-bot: enqueue: probe-slice-run( slice=dialog_short_factual_01, variants=[fp8,int8,gptq,awq], repeat=3 ) — expected ETA 2h.

alex: nice. one more thing — sampling diversity: include a short-tail and long-tail mix so we can see where quantization fails (edge vs typical). maybe 70/30 typical/edge?

mia: +1 to 70/30. also add a tiny 'canary' set of 25 prompts that historically flip under quant. we keep that as a stability litmus.

sara: will do. i'll post the canonical slice registry link and the seed mapping after the run starts. thanks team. :thumbsup:

dmitri: thanks — this should cut down noise in cross-variant comparisons.

eval-bot: run started 1746329050 — logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1746329050

alex: following logs now. if we see systematic drift for a variant, we can trigger the deeper gptq/awq per-layer analysis.

mia: ok, will monitor accuracy deltas and p99. will report back if anything exceeds 1.5% EM drop or 12ms p99 regression.

sara: ack. leaving this thread open for initial observations.
